single.Alapadma: Symbolism: Fully bloomed lotus. | Usage: Denotes beauty, a village, moonlight, or the sun's rays. Common in Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi.
single.Arala: Symbolism: Bent bow. | Usage: Represents drinking nectar, violent wind, or pride. Used to show the courage of a hero.
single.Ardhachandra: Symbolism: Half Moon. | Usage: Represents phases of the moon, seizing by the throat, or a prayer. Also used for showing a plate or a spear.
single.Ardhapataka: Symbolism: Half Flag. | Usage: Denotes leaves, a board, a river bank, or two things side-by-side.
single.Bhramara: Symbolism: Bee. | Usage: Represents a bee, a parrot, or a crane. Used when depicting nature and birds.
single.Catura: Symbolism: Square / Clever. | Usage: Denotes a small quantity, gold, copper, or being witty. Used in storytelling segments.
single.Chandrakala: Symbolism: Crescent Moon. | Usage: Represents the crescent on Lord Shiva's head, the face, or anything moon-shaped.
single.Hamsapaksa: Symbolism: Swan Wing. | Usage: Denotes the number six, a bridge, making a fence, or covering something.
single.Hamsaya: Symbolism: Swan Face. | Usage: Represents a swan, a pearl, or the wick of a lamp. Very delicate and graceful gesture.
single.Kangula: Symbolism: Fruit / Bell. | Usage: Used to denote a small bell, a variety of fruits, or a blossoming flower.
single.Kapittha: Symbolism: Wood Apple. | Usage: Represents Goddess Lakshmi or Saraswati. Also used for holding a veil or a flower.
single.Kartarinukha: Symbolism: Scissors. | Usage: Denotes separation, lightning, or plundering. Common in depicting dramatic conflict.
single.Katakamukha: Symbolism: Bracelet Opening. | Usage: Used for picking flowers, wearing a pearl necklace, or drawing a bow string.
single.Mayura: Symbolism: Peacock. | Usage: Represents a peacock, a bird, or water ripples. Essential for depicting the beauty of nature.
single.Mrgasirsa: Symbolism: Deer Head. | Usage: Denotes a deer, a female, or a house. Used extensively in Krishna-Leela stories.
single.Mukula: Symbolism: Bud. | Usage: Represents a blossom, eating, or the god of love. Also used for concentrated energy.
single.Musti: Symbolism: Fist. | Usage: Denotes steadfastness, grasping, or a fight. Represents strength and determination.
single.Padmakosa: Symbolism: Lotus Bud. | Usage: Represents a lotus bud, various fruits, or a ritual offering. Symbolizes potential.
single.Pataka: Symbolism: Flag / Victory. | Usage: Denotes clouds, a forest, a river, or the beginning of a dance. The most versatile mudra.
single.Sandamsa: Symbolism: Pincers. | Usage: Denotes the number five, a sacrificial offering, or anxiety. Used for minute actions.
single.Sarpashirsa: Symbolism: Snake Hood. | Usage: Represents a cobra, an elephant's ear, or an athlete's massage. Used for fluid movements.
single.Simhamukha: Symbolism: Lion Face. | Usage: Represents a lion, fragrance, or a drop of water. Symbolizes royalty and power.
single.Suchi: Symbolism: Needle / One. | Usage: Denotes a needle, the number one, or the world. Used for pointing or emphasizing.
single.Sukatunda: Symbolism: Parrot Head. | Usage: Represents a parrot's beak, a shooting arrow, or a mysterious matter.
single.Tamracuda: Symbolism: Red Crested Bird. | Usage: Represents a cock, a crane, or a child. Often used in playful contexts.
single.Tripataka: Symbolism: Triple Flag. | Usage: Denotes a crown, a tree, or the weapon Vajra. Used for auspicious symbols.
single.Trisula: Symbolism: Trident. | Usage: Represents the trident of Lord Shiva, the number three, or a sacred symbol.
single.sikhara: Symbolism: Peak / Spire. | Usage: Represents a bow, a hero, or a pillar. Used for depicting strength and peaks.

two.anjali: Symbolism: Salutation / Respect. | Usage: Both palms joined. Used for greeting elders, deities, or the audience.
two.Bherunda: Symbolism: Pair of Birds. | Usage: Represents a pair of mythical birds or two souls in harmony.
two.Chakra: Symbolism: Discus. | Usage: Represents the Sudarshana Chakra of Lord Vishnu or a rotating wheel.
two.Dola: Symbolism: Swing. | Usage: Hands hang loosely. Represents the start of a dance or a sense of dejection.
two.Garuda: Symbolism: Eagle. | Usage: Interlocked thumbs represent wings. Used for depicting birds or the vahana of Vishnu.
two.kapota: Symbolism: Pigeon. | Usage: Palms joined at sides to form a hollow. Denotes politeness or acceptance.
two.karkata: Symbolism: Crab. | Usage: Interlocked fingers represent a crowd, stretching, or the animal crab.
two.Kartarisvastika: Symbolism: Crossed Scissors. | Usage: Denotes branches, a hill, or thick trees. Used in landscape descriptions.
two.Katakavardhana: Symbolism: Coronation. | Usage: Crossed wrists with Katakamukha. Used for weddings or royal ceremonies.
two.Katva: Symbolism: Cot / Bed. | Usage: Represents a bed or a palanquin. Used in narrative sequences.
two.Kilaka: Symbolism: Axle / Bond. | Usage: Represents a bond of affection or the spoke of a wheel.
two.Kurma: Symbolism: Tortoise. | Usage: Represents the tortoise avatar of Vishnu or steady concealment.
two.Matsya: Symbolism: Fish. | Usage: Flat hands with extended thumbs. Essential for depicting water life.
two.Nagabandha: Symbolism: Serpent Coil. | Usage: Represents intertwined snakes. Used for depicting Naga deities.
two.Pasa: Symbolism: Rope / Bond. | Usage: Represents a noose, a rope, or a quarrel. Often used in dramatic scenes.
two.puspaputa: Symbolism: Flower Casket. | Usage: Cupped palms for offering flowers, holding water, or receiving blessings.
two.Sakata: Symbolism: Chariot. | Usage: Represents a chariot or the demon Shakatusura in Krishna stories.
two.Sankha: Symbolism: Conch Shell. | Usage: Represents a sacred conch shell or a call to ritual/war.
two.Sivalinga: Symbolism: Shiva Linga. | Usage: Shikara on a flat palm. Symbolizes the cosmic pillar of Lord Shiva.
two.svastika: Symbolism: Cross / Auspicious. | Usage: Crossed wrists denoting a crocodile or an intense argument.
two.Utsanga: Symbolism: Embrace / Modesty. | Usage: Denotes a respectful embrace or a sense of humility.
two.Varaha: Symbolism: Boar. | Usage: Represents the Varaha avatar of Vishnu or a tusked wild animal.
